373825.title: Liu–Zhang–Zhang conjecture on packing colorings of subcubic graphs
373825.statement: A packing $(1,1,2,2)$-coloring of a graph is a partition of its vertex set into four classes whose pairwise vertex distances are respectively at least $2$, $2$, $3$, and $3$. **Liu–Zhang–Zhang conjecture.** Every connected subcubic graph except the Petersen graph is packing $(1,1,2,2)$-colorable. The supplied text presents this as a stronger conjecture related to the subdivision conjecture, and the current status is not specified there.

373859.title: Existence and non-degeneracy conjecture for the Steklov maximizer among convex polygons
373859.statement:
Let

$$
\mathcal{C}_{N}=\{\Omega\in\mathbb{R}^2:\Omega\text{ is a convex polygon with at most }N\text{ sides and }\operatorname{Per}(\Omega)=2\pi\},
$$

where $\operatorname{Per}(\Omega)$ denotes the perimeter, and let $\sigma_1(\Omega)$ be the first nonzero Steklov eigenvalue. Define

$$
\sigma^*(N):=\sup_{\Omega\in\mathcal{C}_{N}}\sigma_1(\Omega).
$$

**Existence and non-degeneracy conjecture.** The supremum is attained by a convex polygon $\Omega^*$ with exactly $N$ sides. In particular, the maximizer cannot be a degenerate polygon with fewer than $N$ sides.
This conjecture asserts existence of an extremizer in the fixed-perimeter class and rules out loss of sides through degeneration. The supplied context gives no resolution status.

373859.finding: v1 Conjecture 1.1 asks existence and exactly N sides; v2 instead states the stronger polygonal extremal conjecture. Regular-polygon monotonicity does not prove global shape optimization.
373859.remaining_gap: Uniform polygonal compactness with exclusion of loss of sides; no finite certificate route.

373932.title: The odd-graph Thurston–Bennequin symmetry conjecture
373932.statement: Let $O_n$ denote the odd graph with parameter $n\geq 2$. A graph is **TB-symmetrical** when its total Thurston–Bennequin number admits the symmetry described in the paper. **Odd-graph TB-symmetry conjecture.** The odd graph $O_n$ is TB-symmetrical for any $n\geq 2$. This conjecture concerns the classification of TB-symmetrical graphs; it is resolved for $n=2,3$, while the general case remains open.

374103.title: The gamma lower-bound conjecture for weak saturation of hypergraphs
374103.statement:
Let $r\ge 2$, $s\ge 2$, and $k\ge r+1$ be integers. Let

$$
\delta=\binom{k-s+1}{r-s+1}.
$$

Let $H$ be an $r$-uniform hypergraph with $s(H)=s$ and $\delta_{s-1}(H)=\delta$. **The gamma lower-bound conjecture.** Then

$$
\gamma_{s,H}\ge \frac{\delta}{\binom{r}{s-1}}-\frac{1}{\binom{k}{s-1}}.
$$

This would sharpen the general lower bounds for weak saturation in the specified parameter regime; the source suggests proving it using methods analogous to those used for the existing lower bound on $\gamma_{s,H}$.

374204.title: Dai–Zhang–Broerama–Zhang conjecture on Hamiltonicity of connected K_{1,r}-free split graphs
374204.statement:
Let $r$ be an integer with $r\ge 3$. A graph is **$K_{1,r}$-free** if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $K_{1,r}$, and a graph is **Hamiltonian** if it contains a cycle containing all its vertices. A graph is $k$-connected if deleting fewer than $k$ vertices leaves it connected.

**Dai–Zhang–Broerama–Zhang conjecture.** Every $(r-1)$-connected $K_{1,r}$-free split graph is Hamiltonian.

The conjecture extends the known cases $r=3$, where it follows from the characterization of Hamiltonian claw-free split graphs, and $r=4$, established by Dai, Zhang, Broerama and Zhang. Its validity for general $r\ge 3$ is not resolved in the supplied source.

374225.title: Bender et al.'s isomorphism conjecture for uniquely complemented zero-divisor graphs
374225.statement:
Let $S$ be a commutative semigroup with $0$, and let $G(S)$ be its zero-divisor graph. A graph is **uniquely complemented** if it is complemented and any two complements of the same vertex have equal neighborhoods. A vertex has a **unique complement** when it has exactly one complement. Let $\mathcal{P}(n)$ be the semigroup given by the power set of an $n$-element set under intersection.

**Bender et al.'s conjecture.** If $G(S)$ is uniquely complemented with clique number $3$ or greater and every vertex has a unique complement, then $G(S)$ is isomorphic to $G(\mathcal{P}(n))$, where $n$ is the clique number of $G(S)$.

This is one of three conjectures attributed in the source to C. Bender et al. The supplied material gives no evidence that the statement has been resolved.

374250.title: Completeness conjecture for regular Inverse Treblecross positions
374250.statement:
Let $R$ be the regular set of board states, let a state have at most one piece, and let $\mathcal{G}$ denote its Sprague–Grundy value. **Completeness conjecture.** The regular set $R$ contains all board states that possess at most one piece and satisfy $\mathcal{G} \le 1$, with exactly four isolated exceptions:

$$
[1 X 1],\quad [1 X 4],\quad [4 X 1],\quad \text{and}\quad [4 X 4].
$$

These four states are described as isolated anomalies, and empirical data indicates that all other sufficiently long states in their residue classes have $\mathcal{G}>1$; the completeness of $R$ beyond the stated exceptions remains unproved.

374340.title: The mixed edge-deletion conjecture for majority C-chromatic edge-critical graphs
374340.statement:
Let $G$ be an $\overline{\chi}_{\geqslant}$-edge-critical graph with at least two edges, and let $e,f\in E(G)$. **The mixed edge-deletion conjecture.** It is impossible that

$$
\overline{\chi}_{\geqslant}(G-e)<\overline{\chi}_{\geqslant}(G)<\overline{\chi}_{\geqslant}(G-f).
$$

The claim concerns whether edge deletions from an edge-critical graph can produce both a decrease and an increase in the majority $C$-chromatic number. The supplied text does not state whether this has been resolved.
374340.finding: Exhaustive small graph DP plus 3000 larger seeded samples; no mixed critical witness.

374385.title: Fazekas–Mammoliti–Mercaş–Simpson extension of the Fici–Saarela conjecture
374385.statement:
Let $w$ be a binary word of length $n$. An **abelian square** is a factor consisting of two consecutive factors with the same Parikh vector. An abelian square of the form $a^{2i}$ or $b^{2i}$, for a positive integer $i$, is called **trivial**.

**Fazekas–Mammoliti–Mercaş–Simpson conjecture.** A binary word of length $n$ contains at least

$$
\left\lfloor \frac{n}{4}\right\rfloor
$$

abelian squares, and if it contains exactly $\left\lfloor \frac{n}{4}\right\rfloor$ abelian squares, then all the abelian squares are trivial.

This is presented as an extension of the Fici–Saarela conjecture. The supplied text gives no resolution of either the lower bound in full generality or the equality characterization.

374386.title: Lower bound for abelian squares from effective partitions
374386.statement:
Let $w$ be a non-boundary binary word. For a positive integer, write $e(r)$ for the effective partition notation used in the source, and suppose

$$
e(|w|_a)=[i,k],\qquad e(|w|_b)=[j,k].
$$

An **abelian square** is a factor consisting of two consecutive factors with the same Parikh vector.

**Effective-partition conjecture.** The word $w$ contains at least

$$
\left\lfloor \frac{i}{2}\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor \frac{j}{2}\right\rfloor
$$

abelian squares.

The supplied context does not define the notation $e$ or explain whether this assertion is intended as a conjecture beyond the displayed candidate; the status is therefore left open.

374464.title: Kirillov's eventual polynomiality conjecture for stretched Schubert coefficients
374464.statement:
Let $u,v,w\in S_n$. For $N\geq 1$, let $f_{u,v,w}(N)$ denote the stretched Schubert structure coefficient defined in the paper.

**Kirillov's conjecture.** $f_{u,v,w}(N)$ is eventually polynomial in $N$.

Kirillov's conjecture is equivalent to the generating function $P_{u,v,w}(t)$ having no pole other than $t=1$. The paper proves only eventual quasi-polynomiality, equivalently that all poles of $P_{u,v,w}(t)$ are roots of unity, so the stronger polynomiality statement remains open.

374480.title: Planar graph moduli and unlabeled configuration space conjecture
374480.statement:
Let $\mathcal N_n(\mathbb R^2)$ be the moduli space of planar graphs with $n$ bounded faces, and let $\operatorname{uConf}_n(\mathbb R^2)$ be the configuration space of $n$ unlabeled points in the plane. **Planar graph configuration-space conjecture.** There is a homotopy equivalence

$$
\mathcal N_n(\mathbb R^2)\simeq \operatorname{uConf}_n(\mathbb R^2).
$$

The source describes this as a simpler two-dimensional combinatorial parallel and says that no proof was found in the literature.
374480.finding: The source gives a fundamental-group inclusion in an annular moduli setting; it does not identify the full planar graph moduli space with unlabeled configurations. No finite graph enumeration can establish this homotopy equivalence.

374492.title: Engbers–Erey's extremal conjecture for average maximal matching size in trees
374492.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree of order $n$ and diameter $d$. For integers satisfying $d\geq 3$ and $d\neq 4$, write $S_n(1^{n-d},(d-1)^{(1)})$ for the star-like tree specified by the source.

**Engbers–Erey's conjecture.** The average size of maximal matchings, $avm(T)$, is uniquely minimized by

$$
S_n(1^{n-d},(d-1)^{(1)}).
$$

This conjecture concerns the extremal value of the average size of maximal matchings among trees with prescribed order and diameter. The cited context states that the corresponding extremal graphs were known for trees of diameter at most five, while this assertion addresses the remaining specified diameters; its resolution is not given here.

374731.title: The product criterion for Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs
374731.statement:
Let $C_{n_1}(R_1)$ and $C_{n_2}(R_2)$ be circulant graphs such that

$$
C_{n_1}(R_1)\Box C_{n_2}(R_2)=C_{n_1n_2}(R)
$$

for some $R$. **Product criterion conjecture.** The graph $C_{n_1n_2}(R)$ has Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs if and only if at least one of $C_{n_1}(R_1)$ and $C_{n_2}(R_2)$ has Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs. This conjecture is proposed as a consequence of problems 3.1, 3.3, 4.1, and 4.3; its resolution is not specified in the source.

374860.title: The MDS Conjecture for linear codes
374860.statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power, let $C$ be an $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear MDS code of dimension $k$, and let $R$ denote its length. If $k\leq q$, then

$$
R\leq\begin{cases}q+2&\text{if }q=2^h\text{ and }k\in\{3,q-1\},\\q+1&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
$$

**MDS Conjecture.** The stated upper bound holds for the length $R$ of $C$. Despite significant progress, the MDS Conjecture remains open in general for larger values of $k$ and $q$.

374885.title: Signed 4-choosability of planar graphs of girth at least 4
374885.statement: Let $(G,\sigma)$ be a signed planar graph, meaning that $G$ is a planar graph equipped with a signature $\sigma$. Its girth is the length of its shortest cycle. **Girth-four signed choosability conjecture.** Every signed planar graph of girth at least $4$ is signed $4$-choosable. This would improve the known upper bound for signed planar graphs of girth at least $5$, for which the source asks whether the signed list chromatic number is $3$; the conjecture itself is presented as an open problem.

374894.title: Edge-localized Turán inequality for the signless Laplacian spectral radius
374894.statement:
Let $G$) be a connected graph, let $E(G)$ be its edge set, let $\deg(u)$ denote the degree of a vertex $u$, let $q(G)$ denote the spectral radius of the signless Laplacian of $G$, and let $c(uv)$ denote the relevant clique parameter associated with the edge $uv$. **Edge-localized Turán conjecture.**
For any connected graph $G$,

$$
q(G)\le 2\sum_{uv\in E(G)}\left(1-\frac{1}{c(uv)}\right)\left(\frac{1}{\deg(u)} + \frac{1}{\deg(v)}\right).
$$

This is proposed as an edge-localized analogue of a Turán-type inequality for the signless Laplacian. The supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.

374904.title: The half-degree matching-removability conjecture
374904.statement: For $k\ge 1$, a vertex set $S$ in a $k$-connected graph $G$ is **$k$-removable** when $G-S$ remains $k$-connected; a matching is $k$-removable when its edge deletion leaves a $k$-connected graph. **The half-degree matching-removability conjecture.** Every $k$-connected graph $G$ with $\delta(G)\ge k+1$ contains a $k$-removable $\lceil(\delta(G)+1)/2\rceil$-matching, unless $\delta(G)$ is even and $G\cong K_{\delta(G)+1}$. The paper's theorem supports this for $k\le 3$, except for the case $k=3$ and $\delta(G)=4$; the general conjecture remains open.
374904.finding: Matching deletion means edge deletion, not vertex deletion. Exact small graph checks through order 7, with complete even-degree exception removed, gave no witness. Most small regimes are already source-proved.

375027.title: The ordinary-partition containment conjecture
375027.statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be the set of partitions, let $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{2reg}}$ be the set of 2-regular partitions, and let $\operatorname{ORD}:\mathcal{P}\rightarrow\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{2reg}}$ be the function defined from the first column of the spar tableau. If $\lambda,\nu\in\mathcal{P}$ and $\nu$ is obtained by deleting the last row of $\lambda$, then **ordinary-partition containment conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{ORD}(\nu)\subseteq\operatorname{ORD}(\lambda).
$$

This conjecture concerns the behavior of the ordinary-partition function under deletion of a row and is used to support corresponding containment statements for the associated crystal combinatorics.

375053.title: Wang–Qin–Xia's stability conjecture for nontrivial graph pairs
375053.statement: Let $(\Gamma,\Sigma)$ be a **nontrivial graph pair**, meaning that $\Gamma$ and $\Sigma$ are coprime connected twin-free graphs and exactly one of them is bipartite. Assume that the graphs have no loops and that $\Sigma$ is bipartite. **Wang–Qin–Xia's conjecture.** The pair $(\Gamma,\Sigma)$ is stable if and only if $\Gamma$ is stable. This conjecture asks when stability of a nontrivial graph pair reduces to stability of its non-bipartite factor; the supplied source gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
